voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: York, Roman Britain, around the year one hundred and eight. The Ninth Legion is based here. Then it slips out of the record.
Its last securely dated trace in Britain is a stone, carved for a gate of its fortress.
By the one hundred and twenties, the Sixth Legion was at York.
Tiles stamped with the Ninth's name turned up at Nijmegen, in the Netherlands. When they were made is disputed.
Later lists of Rome's legions leave it out. Lost in Britain? Moved to the Rhine? Sent east? No agreed answer.
